title: Hey guys! Here's how I automated background removal for the sprites in my app. (Free, OpenSource)
author: nosy_rhino
selftext:
First off, "what a time to be alive!"

This tool is [**NanoAlpha**](https://nanoalpha.collider.hr/):  
  
**- Free**  
**- Open source**  
**- No login required**  
**- Runs locally (no data collection, no uploads)**

I was working on a 2D mobile game that's using a lot of character sprites and what I found was, that for me at least, chatGPT generates great initial characters based on the description that I give it and can also do pretty nice transparent backgrounds.

But once you have the character in place, making small adjustments like different emotions or poses is nearly impossible without something like nano banana.

The problem with nano banana is that it can't remove the background (at least that I know of), so of course I went down the rabbit hole of using a bunch of different SaaS solutions, created bunch of different accounts, used up all the free tier credits etc.

But to my surprise, none of these tools did the job perfectly, meaning I still had to go into photoshop/gimp and fix the sprites manually, which was tedious.

I later stumbled upon an article that had a neat approach to fix this problem:  
  
Instead of one, you generate 2 identical images with nano banana, first image on one solid color background (for example white) and a second on a contrasting solid color background (black), then using some simple image processing algos, you can get a much better result at removing the background.

And I ended up creating a tool that I used locally to do just that and it worked great!  
So now I've decided to deploy it and share it.

So here you go guys, it's free to use, modify and share.

[https://nanoalpha.collider.hr/](https://nanoalpha.collider.hr/)

[https://github.com/MarkoUnity/NanoAlpha](https://github.com/MarkoUnity/NanoAlpha)

I wish you all **great success** \**obligatory Borat accent*\*, in your game development journey!

P.S. I added a shameful bit of self promotion at the bottom of the page for my app, but if you find it offensive, you can just run the tool locally on your machine :D
